title: NP completeness of bounded machine acceptance
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-code scheme whose canonizer has a polynomially bounded running-time function. The language of strings that can be written as $\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle 1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle$, where $1^m$ denotes a string of $m$ ones, and for which there is a string $u$ of length $n$ such that the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts after exactly $t$ steps on input $\langle x,u\rangle$ and outputs the single bit $1$, is NP-complete.
hypotheses_covered: The canonizer running-time function of $c$ is polynomially bounded
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-code scheme with a canonizer whose running-time bound is
polynomially bounded. Then the language of strings encoding a machine description, an
input, and unary bounds $n,t$, for which some word $u$ of length $n$ makes the decoded
machine halt within $t$ steps on the paired input and output the bit $1$, is
NP-complete.
